publicCase.title: A Rather Final Dinner at Ashby Hall
publicCase.place: Ashby Hall, a creaking country house in the Cotswolds
publicCase.intro: Rain hammers the windows of Ashby Hall. The bridge is out, the telephone is dead, and the soup was only lukewarm. Then things got worse. Lady Constance Ashby was found in the Kitchen, quite dead, her teacup still perfectly level. It happened at 9:30 pm, give or take a biscuit. Five guests are still in the house. One of them did it, and every one of them has a story ready.
briefing: Ashby Hall, November 1932. The bridge is out, the phone is dead, and the soup was lukewarm.
Lady Constance Ashby was found dead in the Kitchen at 9:30 pm.
Seven rooms, a few doors. Nobody walks through walls, not even the guilty.
Mrs Pargeter: secret recipes, secret resentments. Algy: charming, broke, and desperate.
Dr Bligh: steady pulse, shaky past. Colonel Hargreaves: loud stories, quiet debts.

victim.name: Lady Constance Ashby
victim.description: Matriarch of Ashby Hall. Collector of grudges and very small dogs.

suspects.name: Mrs. Dolly Pargeter
suspects.motive: Lady Constance was about to replace her with a fancy chef from Paris.

suspects.name: Algernon Pike
suspects.motive: Lady Constance cut him out of the will last Tuesday.

suspects.name: Dr. Harriet Bligh
suspects.motive: Lady Constance owed her three years of unpaid house calls.

suspects.name: Colonel Rupert Hargreaves
suspects.motive: Lady Constance told everyone the Colonel spent the war in a supply depot. He did.

suspects.name: Hugo Mysterio
suspects.motive: Lady Constance was his biggest investor, and wanted the money back.

boardClues.title: Colonel Hargreaves's little secret
boardClues.text: Colonel Rupert Hargreaves claims to have been in the Great Hall at 8:00 pm. Not so: Colonel Hargreaves was in the Dining Room, caught swapping the place cards to sit next to a secret crush. Mortifying, yes. Criminal, no.
boardClues.short: Colonel Hargreaves fibbed about 8:00 pm: really in the Dining Room

boardClues.title: The croquet mallet
boardClues.text: The Great Hall was tidied at 10:00 pm. The croquet mallet was there, exactly where it always is.
boardClues.short: The croquet mallet, still in the Great Hall at 10:00 pm

boardClues.title: Algy's little secret
boardClues.text: Fresh evidence: at 8:30 pm Algernon Pike was in the Great Hall, sliding down the banister. Not the Dining Room, whatever Algy may say.
boardClues.short: Algy fibbed about 8:30 pm: really in the Great Hall

boardClues.title: An alibi wobbles
boardClues.text: Mrs. Dolly Pargeter claims to have spent 9:30 pm in the Dining Room. But at 9:30 pm nobody was in the Dining Room: the door was still wedged shut with yesterday's newspaper.
boardClues.short: No sign of Mrs Pargeter in the Dining Room at 9:30 pm

boardClues.title: An empty room
boardClues.text: Nobody was in the Dining Room at 9:30 pm: the dust on the floor shows not a single footprint. So Hugo Mysterio was not there either.
boardClues.short: The Dining Room stood empty at 9:30 pm. No Mysterio

boardClues.title: An empty room
boardClues.text: Nobody was in the Kitchen at 8:00 pm: the lamps were off and the cat was asleep on the only chair. So Dr. Harriet Bligh was not there either.
boardClues.short: The Kitchen stood empty at 8:00 pm. No Dr Bligh

safeLies.text: I'm almost certain I saw Algernon Pike in the Dining Room at 8:00 pm.
I'm almost certain I saw Hugo Mysterio in the Great Hall at 10:00 pm.
I'm almost certain I saw Dr. Harriet Bligh in the Conservatory at 9:30 pm.

proofChain.says: Dr. Harriet Bligh and Colonel Rupert Hargreaves were together in the Study at 10:00 pm.
proofChain.therefore: Put that together with what we know, and Dr. Harriet Bligh and Colonel Rupert Hargreaves are in the clear.

proofChain.says: Algernon Pike was in the Great Hall at 9:30 pm.
proofChain.therefore: So Algernon Pike was elsewhere at 9:30 pm, and could not have done it.

proofChain.says: Hugo Mysterio was in the Great Hall at 9:30 pm.
proofChain.therefore: So Hugo Mysterio was elsewhere at 9:30 pm, and could not have done it.

proofChain.says: The croquet mallet was in the Great Hall at 10:00 pm.
proofChain.therefore: So the croquet mallet could not have been in the Kitchen at 9:30 pm. It was not used.

proofChain.says: The silk dressing gown cord was in the Library at 9:00 pm.
proofChain.therefore: So the silk dressing gown cord could not have been in the Kitchen at 9:30 pm. It was not used.

proofChain.says: The bottle of sleeping draught was in the Pantry at 9:00 pm.
proofChain.therefore: On its own it proves nothing. Hold on to it.

proofChain.says: Mrs. Dolly Pargeter and Algernon Pike were together in the Dining Room at 9:00 pm.
proofChain.therefore: So the bottle of sleeping draught could not have been in the Kitchen at 9:30 pm. It was not used.

proofChain.says: Mrs. Dolly Pargeter was not in the Dining Room at 9:30 pm.
proofChain.therefore: So Mrs. Dolly Pargeter lied about 9:30 pm. Everyone else is ruled out. Mrs. Dolly Pargeter took the decanter of port from the Dining Room and was in the Kitchen at 9:30 pm.

confession: Thirty years I fed Lady Constance. Thirty years of soup, and not one word of thanks. Not one.
At 9:30 pm I was in the Kitchen, the decanter of port from the Dining Room in hand. All very quiet.
Do spell my name correctly in the papers.
